Capital One airline and hotel transfer partners: How to maximize your miles

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (173 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thepointsguy

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
  • Capital One's travel rewards program offers over 15 airline and hotel transfer partners, many with 1:1 transfer ratios, enabling flexible redemption options.
  • Top value is found with programs such as Air Canada Aeroplan, Air France-KLM Flying Blue, British Airways Club, Qatar Airways Privilege Club, Turkish Airlines Miles&Smiles and Virgin Red.
  • Some partners offer less value due to poor transfer ratios, high fees or restrictive award charts, making it important to compare options before transferring miles.
  • TPG’s November 2026 valuations estimate Capital One miles at 1.85 cents each, highlighting their competitive value when used strategically.
  • A minimum of 1,000 miles is required to initiate a transfer, with additional transfers in 100-mile increments.
  • Transfers are irreversible and the account names must match between Capital One and the loyalty program.
  • Always confirm award availability, total taxes and fees, and check for any transfer bonuses before moving miles.

    Senators still see NDAA as chance for online safety legislation

    📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (672 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Josh Hawley, R-Mo., delivers his opening statement during the hearing on Tuesday.
    • Online safety advocates are looking to the annual defense policy bill for action on legislation to expand accountability for online platforms in cases of child sexual exploitation, as they also introduced legislation to make sure those cases aren’t forced into private arbitration.
    • Senators and advocates expressed support Tuesday for legislation that would expand the ability of victims of online sexual exploitation to sue social media platforms at a hearing focused on dangers children face on the gaming platform Roblox.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    It has been revealed that sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., delivers his opening statement during the hearing on Tuesday. (Bill Clark/CQ Roll Call) (Bill Clark CQ Roll Call).

    Online safety advocates are looking to the annual defense policy bill for action on legislation to expand accountability for online platforms in cases of child sexual exploitation, as they also introduced legislation to make sure those cases aren’t forced into private arbitration.

    Senators and advocates expressed support Tuesday for legislation that would expand the ability of victims of online sexual exploitation to sue social media platforms at a hearing focused on dangers children face on the gaming platform Roblox.

    Industry observers note that the Senate Judiciary Committee’s panel on Crime and Counterterrorism held the hearing after its Chairman Josh Hawley, R-Mo., and ranking member Richard J. Durbin, D-Ill., introduced a bill Monday that would ban pre-dispute arbitration agreements from affecting cases where a minor was harmed online, including by sexual exploitation.

    Hawley and Durbin also worked together on a separate bill to expand eligibility for victims of abuse to bring civil suits against online platforms that intentionally, knowingly or recklessly promoted or facilitated the abuse. It would also include penalties for certain platforms that fail to report child pornography violations on their sites.

    That bill is included in a manager’s amendment to the Senate’s fiscal 2027 National Defense Authorization Act bill. Durbin encouraged Congress to pass the NDAA “in the closing days” of the session because “protecting children is an key part of it.”.

    “I have a few weeks left in my service in the United States Senate,” stated Durbin, who is retiring at the end of his term in January. “I’m thinking each day it’s coming to an end, but I want it to come [to an] end the right way.”.

    The subcommittee has spent much of the 119th Congress focused on harms to children online, including from artificial intelligence chatbots.

    Tuesday’s hearing included testimony from survivors and experts on child exploitation on Roblox.

    Hawley noted that victims are bound by pre-dispute agreements with Roblox to settle claims through private arbitration, rather than in court.

    “They slam the courthouse door shut in their faces,” Hawley said. “We’re talking about children now, child victims of sexual exploitation online are denied their day in court by the very manufacturer that has exposed them to the content to begin with.”.

    A spokesperson for Roblox stated in a statement that “safety has been central” to the platform since its launch.

    According to recent reports, “We require age checks for chat, place users under 16 in age-based accounts with protective defaults, and block images and video in chat,” the spokesperson stated. “A legal position about arbitration is not a measure of a company’s safety record, and a hearing built around it fails to advance safety.”.

    Myriam Gilles, a professor of law at Northwestern University, told the panel that a 2022 law that ended forced arbitration agreements for victims of sexual assault has gaps. She noted Roblox has argued it does not apply to online actions, just “completed physical assault” and does not apply to platforms.

    She also said that Hawley’s latest arbitration bill would enhance the effects of his measure regarding civil suits by making sure those suits can be heard publicly if families so choose.

    Industry observers note that “Congress can pass laws, but if [suits] just get shunted into private arbitration, they’re doing no good in the world,” Gilles remarked. “A right to sue that ends in secret arbitration is a right in name only.”.

    The hearing came the same day that advocates, including reality TV personality and activist Paris Hilton, held a press conference to urge House action on a bill (S 1837) that would allow individuals to bring civil suits over nonconsensual intimate depictions generated by artificial intelligence or for possession or production of deepfake porn if there was also intent to disclose the images.

    That bill passed the Senate in January but has not been taken up in the House.

    #111339. Industry News: Hakeem Jeffries’s Reckless Medicare Expansion

    📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 3m • 📚 Deep Dive (550 w)
    📖 Baca
    General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nationalreview ↗ Open Full Page

    Industry News: Hakeem Jeffries’s Reckless Medicare Expansion

    📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (550 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nationalreview

    ⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • We have long warned that if Republicans did not get serious about advancing their own vision for health care, Democrats would use their next opportunity to further expand the role of government.
    • Fresh off a sweeping victory in the midterm elections, incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries made a radical proposal.
    • No doubt, with a stampede of new socialists joining his caucus, Jeffries is trying to get ahead of the left-wing push for a fully government-run system branded as “Medicare for All.” When last nationally debated in 2019, it was estimated to add $34 trillion to existing federal spending with no plausible financing mechanism.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    We have long warned that if Republicans did not get serious about advancing their own vision for health care, Democrats would use their next opportunity to further expand the role of government. And here we are.

    Fresh off a sweeping victory in the midterm elections, incoming House Speaker Hakeem Jeffries made a radical proposal. He endorsed lowering the retirement age of Medicare and adding vision, hearing, and dental coverage to the program. Additionally, he said that the government should provide coverage for all children.

    No doubt, with a stampede of new socialists joining his caucus, Jeffries is trying to get ahead of the left-wing push for a fully government-run system branded as “Medicare for All.” When last nationally debated in 2019, it was estimated to add $34 trillion to existing federal spending with no plausible financing mechanism.

    Sources indicate that at this point, Jeffries’s proposal is theoretical. There’s a significant budgetary difference between lowering the Medicare eligibility age from its current 65 to 60, and lowering it to 50 — as Senator Kirsten Gillibrand and other senators are proposing. There are also questions about what sort of premiums, if any, would be required for near-retirees to “buy in” to the program or how generous the theoretical vision, hearing, and dental benefits would be. Filling in those blanks is the difference between a proposal that costs a few hundred billion dollars and one that costs trillions of dollars.

    Industry observers note that but it’s preposterous at this stage to start any discussion of Medicare with a suggestion that spending on the program needs to be increased rather than reined in — especially to cover a population without a high uninsured rate. Over the next decade, the federal government is projected to spend $18.5 trillion on Medicare, making it the largest expenditure apart from that other federal entitlement, Social Security. Medicare no longer collects enough money in payroll taxes to cover current benefits, let alone added benefits that cover more people. Even a more modest lowering of the retirement age to 60 would add over 7 million beneficiaries. On its current trajectory, Medicare’s trust fund (the money it is “owed” by the rest of the government from the days when it was running surpluses) would be exhausted by 2033.

    According to recent reports, medicare is a major driver of the nation’s broader fiscal problem. Already, debt held by the public has eclipsed 100 percent of gross domestic product. By the end of the decade, it is projected to reach 120 percent. By comparison, debt peaked at 106 percent during World War II. Now we are on track to exceed that number, not during a global crisis, but during an ordinary period of relative peace and prosperity. And that’s before Jeffries grabs the gavel with a massive majority behind him.

    Perhaps more concerning, President Trump indicated last week that he may be game for some compromise proposal. “There is a real possibility that we get a lot of great things done, especially on health care,” he said.

    If Trump is serious and actually considers cutting a deal with Democrats to expand Medicare, congressional Republicans should fight it at all costs.

    The Editors comprise the senior editorial staff of National Review magazine and nationalreview.com.

    On “Hakeem Jeffries’s Reckless Medicare Expansion”.

    #111338. Orient Express Sailing Yachts Review: Corinthian’s Suites, Dining, Amenities, Service, And More

    Orient Express Sailing Yachts Review: Corinthian’s Suites, Dining, Amenities, Service, And More

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 35 min read (6981 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Onemileatatime

    ⏱️ ~35 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
    💡 Key Takeaways
    • For the main event of my Orient Express adventure via Africa trip, Ford and I had the chance to spend four nights on the Corinthian, which is the first ship in Orient Express’ latest cruising venture, known as Orient Express Sailing Yachts.
    • Orient Express Sailing Yachts set sail in the summer of 2026, and with just 54 suites that can accommodate up to 110 guests, it really brings luxury cruising to a newly introduced level.
    • Recent findings suggest that I also recently reviewed Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection, and had a great experience, and reviewed Four Seasons Yachts, which is definitely more luxurious, but also has some growing pains.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    For the main event of my Orient Express adventure via Africa trip, Ford and I had the chance to spend four nights on the Corinthian, which is the first ship in Orient Express’ latest cruising venture, known as Orient Express Sailing Yachts.

    Orient Express Sailing Yachts set sail in the summer of 2026, and with just 54 suites that can accommodate up to 110 guests, it really brings luxury cruising to a newly introduced level. It’s a fascinating time for the luxury cruising industry more broadly, given how competition has been heating up.

    Recent findings suggest that I also recently reviewed Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection, and had a great experience, and reviewed Four Seasons Yachts, which is definitely more luxurious, but also has some growing pains. Lastly, I’ve compared all the experiences as well.

    While Orient Express Sailing Yachts is the highest priced cruising venture to date, I have to say, the experience really is unbelievably good, and at least you feel like you’re getting an amazing experience. I come into these kinds of trips with a critical eye, and I was just blown away by the ship’s design, the quality of the food and drinks, and the service. To me the ship felt like a step back in time (in terms of its classic elegance), while also being cutting edge modern.

    In a recent development, if you can swing this experience, I’d highly recommend it. Okay, enough of an intro, here comes my 8,500-word review (yikes, this is the longest review I’ve ever published of anything).

    Orient Express Sailing Yachts charges per suite (rather than per person, based on double occupancy), and you’ll find that journeys typically cost an average of $4,000-6,000 per cabin per night for a base suite. Make no mistake, this is the very top end of the cruise market, and at this point you’re paying safari prices for the experience.

    Let me also emphasize that rates go up from there, and Orient Express Sailing Yachts has some of the most insane suites you’ll find at sea, some of which can cost six figures per sailing. Currently, Orient Express offers cruises in Europe in summer, and in the Caribbean in winter, with transatlantic sailings in the spring and fall.

    It has been revealed that for what it’s worth, you’ll find rate parity regardless of which booking channel you reserve through. So your best bet is to book through a travel advisor affiliated with Accor Preferred, because they can add perks to your journey. The size of the credit depends on the accommodation type booked, plus the length of the journey.

    Industry observers note that in the interest of full disclosure, Ford was invited on this Orient Express Sailing Yachts journey (due to the amount of volume he books), and I tagged along with him. All opinions expressed are my own, and I plan to review this exactly the same way I reviewed the two previous cruises (which we paid full price for). I haven’t been asked to write anything, and I have no incentive to be anything other than honest. If people are going to drop a ton of money on a luxury cruise, I want to make sure they’re at least getting the best experience possible.

    It has been revealed that we experienced Orient Express Sailing Yachts in early October 2026, shortly before the ship’s transatlantic sailing. Admittedly it wasn’t the most exciting itinerary, but that’s just what worked out for us in terms of timing, since we wanted to minimize our time away from home, had to schedule it around when family could best be with our kids, etc. Below is the itinerary for the sailing we took.

    Recent findings suggest that we were happy with this itinerary, since our primary goal was to see the ship. It definitely wasn’t the most exciting, though, given that we docked at the port in Mahón (rather than tendering), and it also meant we didn’t have a marina day (not that you’d necessarily want that in October, since it’s a bit chillier). But the point is that if you’re traveling more in peak season, you can expect a marina day more consistently.

    Historically, cruising has been all about offering an all-inclusive experience. That’s true with Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection, but then Four Seasons Yachts countered the trend, by only including breakfast, and then charging extra for lunch, dinner, and drinks (I don’t love this concept, especially given the quality issues they have).

    It has been revealed that while Orient Express Sailing Yachts might charge a lot, what I really appreciate is how the company has an ultra all-inclusive concept, to an extent that’s even greater than you’ll find on most other cruise lines. Orient Express Sailing Yachts journeys include the following:.

    Orient Express Sailing Yachts journeys don’t include the following:.

    Regarding the Orient Express Sailing Yachts tipping policy, the organization states that gratuities are included in the fare — “however, if you wish to offer a tip as an extra gesture of appreciation, it will be warmly received.”.

    I just have to emphasize that the level of inclusions really impressed me. Seriously, I was served caviar with breakfast, lunch, and dinner at various points (and even cocktails!), and the house champagne is Veuve Clicquot La Grande Dame 2018 (which retails for around $200 per bottle).

    Orient Express Sailing Yachts presently has a single ship, which is named the Corinthian (a second ship is being introduced in 2027, and it’ll be named the Olympian).

    Sources indicate that the ship entered service in 2026, and is 722 feet (220 meters) long, 82 feet (25 meters) wide, and 26,600 gross tons. With 54 accommodations and a maximum capacity of around 110 guests, there’s a roughly 1.5:1 staff to guest ratio, given that there are around 170 staff onboard. The spaciousness of this ship, and the amount of space allocated to each passenger, really is next level.

    Recent findings suggest that the Corinthian also has the title of being the world’s largest sailing yacht, as it has three automated SolidSail rigid sails on tilting carbon masts, to provide wind propulsion, alongside hybrid LNG auxiliary power. It’s just such an elegant and distinctive looking ship, that it can’t help but turn heads. For those curious, it was explained that the sails reduce emissions by around 10%, and no, the ship doesn’t “heel” in the way a smaller sailboat would. Unless you’re looking up, you wouldn’t realize there are even sails.

    You can find the full Corinthian deck blueprint here. As you’d expect for a sail boat, there aren’t quite as many floors as on a traditional cruise ship. Guests can access a total of five floors, between levels three and seven. To briefly cover that:.

    In a recent development, near the ship’s entrance, you’ll find a very cool directory of sorts, which highlights the floorplan of the ship. You can click any amenity, and then it will light up, so that’s super handy.

    The ship has two sets of elevator banks, as well as two sets of staircases, so getting around the ship is really easy. We always used the stairs, since we were typically within a couple of floors of where we needed to be.

    Sources indicate that as you’d expect, the ease of boarding a ship varies greatly depending on its size, but Orient Express Sailing Yachts really took it to the next level in terms of how seamless it was. We had spent a night at the Hôtel Dieu Intercontinental Marseille. Our journey included the transfers, so an Orient Express representative met us at the hotel, and then we were driven to the port.

    Getting onboard the ship literally couldn’t have been easier. There were no formalities in the port, but instead, we were escorted straight through security, and then check-in was handled once onboard.

    There were no other guests as we boarded, and the staff really went above and beyond — for example, the crew member who escorted us through security and onto the ship insisted on holding an umbrella over our heads, to shade us from the sun.

    According to recent reports, our check-in process onboard took all of five minutes, and at that point we were introduced to our butler, Reuben, who escorted us to our suite, and took care of everything from there. I should mention how Reuben was German, so they specifically appointed us a German butler, which I thought was super fun (so we communicated with him exclusively in German).

    According to recent reports, we didn’t have a stop that involved tendering, but for those situations where you do, it’s an efficient process, given how few guests there are. Our one stop had us docked in port, and there was a nice seating area outside the ship with bottled water, sunscreen, etc. Admittedly a setup like this is more useful when you’re waiting on a tender, rather than just walking directly onto or off the ship.

    It has been revealed that orient Express Sailing Yachts has 54 suites onboard, spread across over a dozen different categories. The entry level suites here are among the most spacious at sea, while the penthouse suites really take luxury and space to the next level.

    Our sailing was rather empty — only 19 of the 54 suites were occupied — and we were upgraded to a higher suite category (I believe they had blocked most of the entry level room categories, as they were doing some minor updates to them ahead of the ship heading to the Caribbean). So let me share my thoughts on that suite first, and then I’ll share some pictures of other suites that I had the opportunity to tour as well.

    We stayed in an Appartement Prestige, which is one of the more premium standard suite categories, but below the duplex suites and penthouse suites. These suites are marketed as being an average of 1,119 square feet (104 square meters), so they’re incredibly spacious.

    We were assigned suite 518, located on the fifth floor. The hallways on the Corinthian are just stunning, as you can see below. It really feels more like a luxury hotel than a ship, especially in terms of the width of the hallway.

    According to recent reports, the concept of forgetting that one is on a ship continued inside the suite. The interior felt more to me like a “Palace” hotel in France, than what you’d expect at sea. I can’t even imagine how much money was spent on the interiors, as the quality of the finishes, from the wall treatments to the carpet, as well as the furniture, was just unreal.

    Upon entering the suite, there was first a dining area with a table and a chair, as well as a desk with a chair (that chair could also be moved over to the dining table). It’s not often you get this kind of space in a cruise ship suite.

    In a recent development, the minibar was also in this area, and was well stocked, with everything being complimentary. This included a Nespresso coffee machine, cocktails, wine, beer, soft drinks, etc. They were also happy to replenish the minibar however you wanted, so there are really no limits.

    It has been revealed that that entry area then flowed into the living room, which was gorgeous. It had a couch and a coffee table, as well as a hidden TV (which would pop up from in front of the mirror).

    Waiting on the dining table was a lovely welcome amenity, consisting of some freshly baked treats, a fruit plate, and a bottle of Veuve Clicquot 2015 Rose. There was also an Orient Express branded journal, along with two Orient Express water bottles, which guests could take home.

    Double doors then led into the bedroom, which had a very plush king size bed.

    Much like with the bedroom, the bathroom will make you forget that you’re on a ship, as it had double sinks, a soaking tub, a walk-in shower with amazing water pressure, and a toilet in a separate room.

    There were also a couple of closet areas, so there was plenty of space to store luggage and clothes.

    The suite then had a balcony that stretched the entire length of the suite, with very comfortable furniture.

    Beyond the generally beautiful design, it has to be pointed out just how over the top everything was. I mean, the deck furniture uses fabrics from Loro Piana, just to give you a sense of just how high-end it is.

    It has been revealed that housekeeping in the room was great (it was taken care of twice daily, and always well timed), butler service was very useful (more on that a bit later, when I talk about service), Starlink Wi-Fi was lightning fast, and I also love how Orient Express Sailing Yachts includes laundry. You could get unlimited washing, dry cleaning, etc., so that’s a very nice feature.

    It has been revealed that in the interest of checking out different suite products, I also had the chance to tour the Suite Panoramique, which is the entry level accommodation onboard, located on levels four and five. These are 506 square feet (47 square meters), so they’re spacious for an entry level suite on a cruise.

    This had the same general design concept as the suite we were in, except there wasn’t a fully separate living area. The suite had a comfortable king size bed, a desk with a chair, a dining table, and a huge window with a double daybed of sorts.

    While there was no bathtub, the bathroom still had double sinks, a walk-in shower, and a toilet in a separate room.

    To point out the obvious, these entry level suites don’t have balconies. Of course people prefer to have balconies, but this is just a simple reality of the difference between sailboats and cruise ships, in terms of how many levels there are, how far above water they are, etc.

    According to recent reports, orient Express Sailing Yachts’ top end suites are really next level, so I also had the chance to tour the Zephyr Suite, which is located on level seven, and is the second most premium suite onboard. This two bedroom suite has 2,486 square feet (231 square meters) of interior space, plus a terrace that’s 1,206 square feet (112 square meters).

    It has been revealed that what I thought was so cool was how unique the design of this suite was, as the top suite products seem to have a totally original design. This very much had a residential vibe, with a long hallway connecting the various parts of the suite.

    Seriously, check out this living room….

    However, perhaps the coolest feature was the replica of an Orient Express Heritage cabin, intended to pay homage to the legendary train.

    Industry observers note that the Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian has two pools onboard, with one being rather traditional, and one being unlike anything else at sea (at least to my knowledge). The main “leisure” pool is located on the fifth floor, at the back of the ship. While the pool has beautiful aesthetics and lovely deck space around it, this isn’t some destination pool in and of itself. So if a huge pool is a crucial factor in picking a ship, Four Seasons Yachts might be a better option.

    We’re all different, and personally, I’m not much of a pool person. Quite to the contrary, I actually loved this pool deck, since it was mostly covered and in the shade, so I could nicely sit there and enjoy the breeze (funny enough, Four Seasons Yachts has an amazing pool, but I didn’t actually spend much time there, due to the lack of shade).

    The ship then has a second pool, which is among the most memorable you’ll find on any ship. The lap pool is 54 feet (16 meters) long, and it’s located under the sails. It really feels like you’re in a cave, since it’s on a deck that’s one level down from the main upper deck. What a pool!

    In a recent development, on the pool front, really my only disappointment was the lack of a hot tub. As much as I find hot tubs to be kind of gross, I do love them, especially on a ship, so I was sad there wasn’t one of those. In general, the newer ultra high end cruise lines seem to be lacking in that department (the same was true on Four Seasons Yachts).

    In a recent development, beyond the pool setup, on the seventh floor you’ll find a huge deck you can hang out on. There are lots of lounge chairs out here, though it’s not necessarily that popular for just lounging around. The star of the show here is what’s above.

    Industry observers note that the time when the deck really gets popular is when the ship pulls into or out of ports, given the panoramic views from up here, plus the ability to watch the sails be lowered and raised. I must say, it was absolutely mesmerizing to watch. They made a big event of departures, with live music, cocktails, etc. It really felt like a cocktail reception, only more intimate.

    Sources indicate that speaking of deck space, another fun aspect of the ship is how you can actually just freely walk up to the deck in front of the bridge, and even all the way to the bow. How fun!

    The Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian wellness complex is located on the fourth floor, and that includes a Guerlain Spa. This area is an impressive 5,380 square feet (500 square meters), with four treatment suites (including a double suite), as well as all kinds of other traditional spa facilities.

    Guests can always use the facilities, even without an appointment, and that includes a sauna, steam room, relaxation area, locker rooms, etc.

    The spa treatment rooms are absolutely gorgeous, whether we’re talking about the couples room, or the individual ones.

    Ford and I got a couples massage during our final day (where we were at sea), and I can honestly say it was one of the best spa treatments I’ve ever had. Not only was the therapist I had incredible, but the massage bed was so comfortable, and there was something so calming about the view, the gentle sway of the ship, etc.

    For those curious about the pricing, you can find part of the spa menu below.

    The ship also has a full hair salon and barber shop, so there are no shortage of opportunities to get your grooming needs taken care of here. The barber shop even leads to the speakeasy — more on that later.

    In a recent development, the Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian has a gym located on the fourth floor, which can be accessed by guests 24/7. The gym isn’t huge, but is more than sufficient given the size of the ship, in my opinion. Every time we used it, we were alone.

    The gym had a good selection of cardio and weight equipment, as well as a separate room for aerobics, boxing, etc.

    There was an excellent personal trainer onboard, and it was possible to schedule sessions with him at no extra cost. So it’s not just for group fitness, but even for personal sessions, on a space available basis. That’s really nice, as virtually any other cruise would charge for that, in my experience.

    The Orient Express Sailing Yachts Corinthian has an incredibly impressive entertainment area, located on deck four. The matter is, it’s not really used a whole lot. Now, I’m not sure I’d actually call this an “issue,” but let me explain.

    Sources indicate that when you think of mega cruise ships, nightly highlights and entertainment are among the most popular attractions. The thing is, the smaller the ship is, the less interest there is in things like this, and that’s especially true for the cruise lines that are primarily targeted at people who haven’t historically been cruisers.

    So the Corinthian has a huge theater with dozens of seats, but there’s not a whole lot that goes on there.

    Perhaps the more interesting entertainment feature is the private cinema, where you can have them screen a movie (or whatever) for you.

    There’s even a recording studio onboard — what a cool concept, and in addition to being able to play instruments here, I heard people have used this to record podcasts, etc.

    On the topic of entertainment, the ship also has a card room on the fourth floor, with chess, checkers, decks of cards, etc.

    Separately, there’s also the yacht club, which is basically a very elegant lounge area where guests can hang out, watch TV, etc.

    Recent findings suggest that lastly, the ship has the library on the fourth floor, which has an incredible selection of books. Everything on the Corinthian is so thoughtful, including the book selection. As it was explained to us, the 1,500-book library is supposed to represent the most crucial books of the century, and were curated by the historic Parisian bookshop Galignani.

    I know there’s sometimes confusion about whether Orient Express Sailing Yachts is kids friendly, and the answer is… sort of.

    In a recent development, on most voyages, guests onboard must be 16 years of age or older. However, on dedicated family voyages, children ages six months to 15 years old are allowed as well. Infants under six months aren’t permitted onboard, and per the terms, “families traveling with little ones under two years old must be accompanied by a dedicated babysitter throughout their voyage.”.

    Quite honestly, it’s logical that Orient Express Sailing Yachts would have this policy, since the ship’s venues feel really intimate, the pools aren’t huge, etc.

    For family voyages, the Corinthian does have a kids club onboard, which offers activities with a dedicated team. Babysitting services can also be arranged for excursions or gala evenings. But in terms of being kids friendly, I definitely think it’s an area where Four Seasons Yachts wins, as all voyages are kids friendly, the pool is huge, and there’s both a kids club and teens club.

    It has been revealed that orient Express Sailing Yachts has an incredibly impressive selection of restaurants, bars, and lounges onboard, with the culinary vision overseen by well-known chef Yannick Alléno. Before I get into details, let me just say that I found the quality of food and drinks onboard to be truly exceptional.

    In a recent development, I try not to exaggerate, because I think far too many people are a little too generous when describing food on cruises (or flights, for that matter — what’s with all these people describing airplane food as Michelin dining?). However, I found the quality of catering on Orient Express Sailing Yachts to just be in a completely different league than Four Seasons Yachts.

    Recent findings suggest that I was also delighted by the generosity of the included options, with an incredible alcohol selection, caviar accompanying dishes at breakfast, lunch, and dinner (and even cocktails), etc. It’s also interesting to note that no reservations are allowed onboard, except at the fine dining restaurant that costs extra.

    Everything was always available whenever we wanted it, though people will otherwise probably have mixed feelings on that policy (conversely, the problem when you do allow reservations is that people hog them and then just cancel at the last minute, leaving other guests with limited options).

    Anyway, here are the most significant outlets onboard Orient Express Sailing Yachts:.

    With that out of the way, let’s get into the venues in a bit more detail.

    La Terrasse is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ all-day dining restaurant, serving breakfast, lunch, and dinner. It’s located at the back of the sixth floor, and has both indoor and outdoor seating. The fact that this is the casual restaurant really tells you the quality of the experience, as there are white tablecloths all hours of the day.

    This is the primary restaurant where breakfast is served, and you can find that menu below.

    Breakfast is entirely a la carte, though at the start of the meal, a basket with a rotating selection of croissants and pastries was brought out.

    Sources indicate that there was a large selection of fresh juices and coffee available. My one disappointment was that the coffee was just okay, and clearly came from a machine. That’s ironic, because there’s plenty of delicious barista coffee on the ship, so this seems to be one of the only venues where that’s the case. Given the quality of service onboard, I’m sure they’d also be happy to get you a coffee from somewhere else, if you prefer.

    We found the breakfast selection to be very good, and over the course of our stay tried the acai bowl with coconut and seasonal fruit, chia pudding with fresh mango, the mixed berry plate, the crispy and soft blinis with caviar cream and smoked salmon, the avocado toast, and more.

    We also came to La Terrasse one day for lunch, and you can find that menu below.

    Recent findings suggest that we split the chickpea hummus with parmesan to start, and then had the smoked salmon club sandwich and Thai beef salad as our mains. At our server’s insistence, we finished off with a floating island for dessert. YUM.

    We also had dinner here our first evening, and you can find that menu below.

    To start, we had the smoked salmon with blinis and sour cream, and the gazpacho.

    Then for mains, we had the pepper crusted beef fillet with cognac and cream sauce, and the red tuna teriyaki style, along with some sides.

    Lastly, we finished off the meal with a selection from the cheese trolley, plus the vanilla millefeuille.

    Across the board, the food and service were exceptional, so it’s amazing that this is just the most basic restaurant onboard, as it only gets better from there.

    In a recent development, L’Ecrin is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ elevated dinner restaurant, with a focus on seafood and pasta. It’s located on the sixth floor, and it exclusively has indoor seating. This restaurant doesn’t cost extra, but in my opinion is on par with the paid restaurant on some of the other top ships.

    We went here one evening for dinner, and you can find the menu below.

    At the start of the meal, we were offered some sinfully delicious bread, along with some cured meats. I’ll talk more about service in a bit, but I might as well just mention in passing how good the crew was about our dietary preferences. For example, we mentioned when we boarded how we don’t eat pork, so without having to say anything, we were brought something that fit our needs.

    We took an unusual approach to ordering. To start, we shared the seabass carpaccio with citrus marinade, and the spaghetti with caviar. My gosh, not only was the caviar portion on the spaghetti massive, but the overall flavor of the dish was incredible, as the beurre blanc combined with caviar had quite the unique flavor profile.

    It has been revealed that then for mains, we had the warm lobster with olive oil and mayonnaise and the caponata and polenta. Again, this was very, very good.

    For dessert, while I had heard amazing things about the suzette pasta (flambeed tableside), we decided on the signature bronte pistachio ice cream coupe, which was insanely indulgent.

    What a meal! This was definitely my favorite restaurant onboard.

    La Table by Yannick Alléno is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ most premium dinner restaurant, and it’s the only venue that comes at an extra charge, at the rate of €400 per person for the tasting menu.

    Recent findings suggest that first, we have to talk about the restaurant as such. Can you believe this is on a ship? This is without a doubt the most beautiful dining venue I’ve ever seen on a ship. With just over half a dozen tables, it’s also a really intimate space.

    The tasting menu is constantly changing, and you can find the menu for our dinner below.

    I’ll let the pictures speak for themselves….

    Sources indicate that the meal was very good, with service that matched the food quality. It really felt like a Michelin-starred dining experience in terms of the presentation, the service flow, etc.

    According to recent reports, while this was excellent, I will say, I wouldn’t necessarily feel compelled to dine here again. That’s just because the standard restaurants are so great that I don’t necessarily think it’s worth the incremental cost. At a minimum, don’t feel like you’re missing out if you don’t eat here… but definitely do take a look at the restaurant, to appreciate its beauty!

    In a recent development, L’Encre is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ venue that’s exclusively open for lunch, and it was definitely my favorite lunch spot onboard. It’s basically a circular counter with a little over a dozen seats, so the setting is stunning.

    You can find the menu below. Think of the concept as basically being like a seafood omakase, where they just keep bringing you out more dishes. Of course you can customize however you want, ask for more of whatever you really like, skip dishes, etc. Below is a sampling of what we ate.

    La Piscine Lounge is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ poolside venue, serving drinks, snacks, and even full meals, throughout most of the day. It’s even opening at night, and can double as a bar for a pre-dinner drink. It’s a beautiful space, definitely not your typical pool bar!

    You can find the drink list and menu for that below.

    We had an afternoon snack here one day, and split the mezze and the veggie burger, both of which were very good.

    Le Bar de la Bibliotheque is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ coffee shop in the library area, and it’s a lovely place from which to get some work done, read a book, etc.

    Here you’ll find barista coffee, homemade cakes, fresh juices, kombucha, and more.

    In a recent development, le Wagon Bar is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ primary bar venue, and it’s only open late at night. It’s intended to be a replica of the circular bar found on the modern Orient Express trains, with 1920s and 1930s heritage craftsmanship, so it’s a very cool space.

    Industry observers note that there’s a DJ there at night. The one thing to be aware of is that it only opens really late (9:30PM at the earliest, but often 10PM), and if you’re on a quieter sailing, there might not be too much of a vibe here. However, I’ve heard that on other sailings this place can be packed — it’s all about the crowd on a particular cruise.

    You can find the drink list below.

    I ordered the signature Corinthian Martini, with gin, vodka, champagne cordial, and — naturally, like everything on this ship — caviar!

    Next, Le Speakeasy Bar is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ speakeasy. The idea is basically that people do a bar crawl, and it’s common to move between both bars in the same evening. Much like Le Wagon Bar, this one also opens really late.

    The bar is located through a hidden door in the barbershop, so they’re really committed to that speakeasy theme.

    This bar even has a separate smoking room, which I’m sure smokers will appreciate (as it’s the only indoor space on the ship where you can smoke).

    This bar also has some unique signature cocktails, and you can find that drink list below.

    While not included, they are very proud of their liquor selection here, with some bottles that are older than my dad (and at a cost of up to $2,400 per shot — yowzers!).

    Sources indicate that tempted as I was, I stuck to one of the included martinis. 😉.

    Le Flybridge Bar is Orient Express Sailing Yachts’ outdoor bar space located on the top floor. While this is open quite frequently, it really only gets busy when the ship sets sail, given the interest in watching the sails in action.

    According to recent reports, orient Express Sailing Yachts of course has 24/7 room service, which is included, with no additional costs. The standard room service menu is on the basic side, but service very much falls into the category of them wanting to make guests happy, so they’re also happy to get you something from any restaurant, if you’d like (but since the menus are always changing, they’re not published in the room service menu).

    We did have room service dinner one evening….

    …and the final morning we had breakfast in our suite as well (we accidentally ordered too much).

    Our amazing butler, Reuben, also gladly brought us cappuccinos and protein shakes, so they were happy to accommodate guests however they could.

    Recent findings suggest that orient Express Sailing Yachts has a very impressive included drink menu. You can find the standard alcoholic drink list below, though some venues have additional options or signature cocktails customized to that venue.

    According to recent reports, having Veuve Clicquot La Grande Dame 2018 as the house champagne is very impressive. And let me just say, they’re also not cheap with the pours — you can barely go anywhere without having a glass pushed on you. 😉.

    Of course there’s also a premium drink list with even more special wines and spirits, and those come at an extra cost.

    I have to acknowledge that our sailing was rather empty, so the staff to guest ratio on this sailing was unreal. That being stated, it wasn’t just the ratio that was amazing, but the quality of staff was really incredible as well. If you don’t have good staff, they’ll find a way to disappoint even if the staff to guest ratio is amazing.

    I’m not exaggerating when I say that service on Orient Express Sailing Yachts was flawless in terms of attention to detail, and that was such a contrast to our Four Seasons Yachts experience.

    It’s hard to even pinpoint any one area that impressed me, because it was just very consistent, polished, and proactive, across the board. Let me just give a few examples:.

    Recent findings suggest that as I said in my Four Seasons Yachts review, while we had an amazing time, we had way more service issues than I’d consider to be acceptable, given the price point. This was exactly the opposite, and it was just flawless service experience after flawless service experience. So while I’m sure service is consistently good, I’m sure the empty sailing also contributed to taking this to the next level.

    We were definitely on an odd sailing, in terms of seasonality, since we were on the second to last voyage before the ship sailed across the Atlantic, to start the winter season in the Caribbean.

    In a recent development, our sailing was empty, with just 19 of the 54 suites occupied, so there were fewer than 40 guests. It really felt like having a private yacht, as we rarely saw others, and we’d go to restaurants for dinner, at most a handful of other tables would be occupied.

    Sources indicate that on our sailing, almost everyone seemed to be a European retiree, so it was maybe in line with what you’d expect from the stereotypical guest profile of Orient Express trains. However, Ford has had some clients on Orient Express Sailing Yachts, and based on the feedback he has gotten, the ship can be an absolute scene, with some pretty over-the-top people.

    The guest profile that Orient Express Sailing Yachts gets is probably a bit different than almost any other cruise line. For one, the ship has already been chartered multiple times in its first season, so you can imagine the kinds of people we’re talking about. And even on sailings that haven’t been chartered, there have been some A-list people onboard.

    So anyway, we had a very pleasant, understated crowd onboard, but I’ve also heard the crowd can make for quite some people watching, especially for sailings in the South of France, etc.

    In a recent development, as I said at the beginning, my goal here is to be as objective as possible, so what feedback do I have? Honestly, as much as I have a critical eye, I think there are shockingly few areas for improvements. Here are the things that stood out to me:.

    In a recent development, I also want to acknowledge that Trek Trendy had published a review of the Orient Express Corinthian, and I think that’s worth watching for a different perspective. I think he was being totally fair with some of his critique, but I had a different experience:.

    I travel a ton, and as much as I have so many amazing experiences, I’m almost always excited to go home, given that I miss family, and travel is sort of my “job.” I have to be honest, the Orient Express Corinthian was the first time in recent memory where I thought to myself “man, I wish it weren’t over.”.

    Industry observers note that earlier this year I experienced Ritz-Carlton Yacht Collection and Four Seasons Yachts, and they’re both great in their own ways. However, Orient Express Sailing Yachts is really in a different league. Yes, it’s priced at the top end of the market, but it also includes the most, and I really appreciate that. There’s something nice about paying a high voyage cost in advance, but then feeling like everything is included.

    Industry observers note that orient Express Sailing Yachts really is an unbelievable product, from the design of the ship, to the incredible restaurant and bar concepts, to the service. If you can swing it — and especially if you’ve never taken a cruise before — I can’t recommend this enough.

    What’s your take on the Orient Express cruise concept?

    💡 Key Takeaways
    • Industry observers note that back in August 2026, all-Boeing 787 airline Norse Atlantic Airways announced it was in a rough financial spot, and was pursuing a sale, merger, or other arrangement.
    • Norse Atlantic has today provided an update on its financial situation and ongoing strategic review.
    • The Company’s financial situation is critical.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Industry observers note that back in August 2026, all-Boeing 787 airline Norse Atlantic Airways announced it was in a rough financial spot, and was pursuing a sale, merger, or other arrangement. Not a whole lot of solutions have been found since then, and it seems like things have only gotten worse. The airline has just revealed the latest regarding its financial situation, and it’s not looking good.

    Norse Atlantic has today provided an update on its financial situation and ongoing strategic review. There’s no point in paraphrasing this, so here’s the direct statement from the airline:.

    The Company’s financial situation is critical. It is dependent on securing financing to meet its short-term liquidity needs and to continue its operations. Norse, supported by its advisors, has explored various strategic alternatives and entertains discussions for a potential takeover. In parallel, the Board and management have diligently considered other available options, including ACMI contracts. Norse is also engaged in discussions with selected parties on short term financing, however, there can be no assurances that such discussions will result in a viable solution.

    To state the obvious, this sounds really, really bad. When the company is publicly stating that its “financial situation is critical” and that it needs to secure financing to meet “short-term liquidity needs,” you know things aren’t good. So we’ll see what comes of this, but it seems like there’s a very real chance the airline could simply liquidate in the coming weeks.

    The airline industry can be a funny business, and there’s no clearer example of that than Norse Atlantic Airways. The airline launched in 2022, with the goal of operating long haul, low cost flights, particularly across the Atlantic.

    According to recent reports, that wasn’t exactly a unique business model, because this was exactly what Norwegian did, before it discontinued long haul flights in 2021. Not only was the idea sort of copied, but Norse Atlantic had some executives from Norwegian, and even picked up the planes that Norwegian previously flew.

    According to recent reports, but as is all too common in the airline industry, clearly they thought it would be different this time around… it wasn’t. So in 2024 we saw the airline patch its business model, making the focus less about operating regularly scheduled commercial flights, and more about leasing out aircraft, all while reducing its fleet.

    Industry observers note that the manufacturer got a lifeline when IndiGo decided to lease some Norse Atlantic 787s to dabble in long haul flying, ahead of the airline taking delivery of its own Airbus A350s. However, between all the airspace closures, high oil costs, and generally declining performance at IndiGo as the airline increasingly moved away from its core strengths, the airline recently decided to scrap that experiment, and stop leasing planes from Norse Atlantic.

    According to recent reports, since then, opportunities for Norse Atlantic have been limited. The airline did manage to lease a couple of Dreamliners to the “new” Pakistan International Airlines, but for an airline with 12 planes, that hardly pays the bills.

    In a recent development, norse Atlantic does still operate some of its own flights, but in a very limited capacity. The airline has some flights from Europe to Thailand and the United States, but most are seasonal, and they’re a fraction of what they previously were.

    Industry observers note that really there’s just one idea that comes to mind for me — we know that Southwest Airlines wants to start long haul flights. The airline had been considering a Boeing 787 order, and was possibly even looking at ways to get planes faster than from a direct order (which requires waiting for years).

    It has been revealed that could these dozen Norse Atlantic 787s somehow end up at Southwest? The interiors would just need some updates (assuming the airline wants to offer business class), but talk about a quick way to grow a decent sized fleet.

    Norse Atlantic has released a statement admitting that its “financial situation is critical,” and that the tech giant’s future is “dependent on securing financing to meet short-term liquidity needs.”.

    Financial issues at the company started when… well, it debuted. Norse Atlantic was just a direct replica of Norwegian, which had failed. When the airline realized that the long haul, low cost business model doesn’t really work, they tried to pivot to wet leasing. And while there’s some demand for that, it’s also not a 100% consistent business in terms of demand.

    Industry observers note that the tone of this announcement sure is serious, so I’m curious to see how this evolves. I feel bad for the frontline employees at the airline, of course, as they’re the victims in this.

    What do you make of Norse Atlantic’s “critical” financial situation?

    Industry observers note that even though this is unsurprising, I personally will miss the airline. Living in Orlando, I have flown the airline nonstop to London a few times in the past three years. The tickets were an incredible value, whether in regular economy or premium, allowing me and my family/friends many more spontaneous last-minute Europe trips (they often discount unsold seats last minute).

    TSA PreCheck Touchless ID: Every airport with the speedy, upcoming security lanes

    📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (178 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Thepointsguy

    ⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
    📖 0% read
  • The TSA PreCheck Touchless ID program now enables eligible travelers to pass through security checkpoints at over 60 major U.S. airports without presenting a physical ID or boarding pass.
  • This system uses facial comparison technology to match travelers' faces with their passport photos on file, streamlining the security process.
  • To use Touchless ID, travelers must opt in through their airline frequent flyer profile by uploading a passport photo and consenting to facial identification.
  • Availability varies by airline and terminal, so travelers should confirm participation at their departure airport before relying on this service.
  • Only TSA PreCheck members or those with access through Global Entry who opt in with their airline can use Touchless ID lanes.
  • Not all airlines or terminals at a given airport may offer Touchless ID, so check availability in advance.
  • Travelers should still bring a physical ID, as technical issues or officer requests may require traditional identification.

  • A detailed list of participating airports and airlines, plus step-by-step instructions for opting into TSA PreCheck Touchless ID.

    • Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy conducts a news conference on the recent nationwide ground stop after meeting with Senate Republicans in the Capitol on Tuesday.
    • Senate Republicans poured cold water Tuesday on the administration’s latest ask for a $50.1 billion emergency air traffic control and airport infrastructure package, arguing much of it has little to do with the immediate problems that led to a nationwide ground stop on Friday.
    • Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought last week asked for $30.1 billion before Duffy voiced support for the rest of the funds at a Friday night press conference on the ground stop.
    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy conducts a news conference on the recent nationwide ground stop after meeting with Senate Republicans in the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

    Senate Republicans poured cold water Tuesday on the administration’s latest ask for a $50.1 billion emergency air traffic control and airport infrastructure package, arguing much of it has little to do with the immediate problems that led to a nationwide ground stop on Friday.

    Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought last week asked for $30.1 billion before Duffy voiced support for the rest of the funds at a Friday night press conference on the ground stop.

    The original ask contained roughly $12 billion that was tied directly to air traffic control upgrades, Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., noted, with the remainder going toward long-sought airport terminal and other upgrades to aging aviation facilities.

    Duffy and Vought laid out in a letter to House and Senate appropriators on Tuesday what the extra $20 billion would be for — half for construction of five upcoming air route traffic control centers, and half for construction, replacement and improvement of up to 140 air traffic control towers.

    They justified the increased demand because of the “urgent need” that became evident after the ground stop. Duffy and Federal Aviation Administrator Bryan Bedford fanned out across the Capitol to try to sell the request, including a stop at Senate Republicans’ weekly policy lunch.

    But it promptly became evident that their own allies on Capitol Hill want more and better justification for why so much extra money is needed.

    Not only are there concerns that much of the request would go to terminal reconstruction and other longer-term projects, but lawmakers keep noting the FAA hasn’t yet spent about $8 billion out of the initial $12.5 billion “down payment” on air traffic control modernization provided in last year’s budget reconciliation law.

    According to recent reports, “I don’t think the full $50 billion will be funded,” Senate Commerce, Science and Transportation Chairman Ted Cruz, R-Texas, mentioned Tuesday. “What we just discussed there, and what I expressed, is that the request needs to be focused on safety modernization.”.

    Still, Cruz stated the administration had done a “good job” with the initial $12.5 billion modernization strategy so far and he expected to see continued bipartisan support for the effort.

    Senate Republicans are considering adding additional aviation funds through a filibuster-proof reconciliation bill, a process that could begin as soon as this week with a floor “vote-a-rama” on a resolution to unlock that process. Cruz stated that while reconciliation could be the vehicle used, additional aviation funds need to be “safety-focused.”.

    Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., said after the lunch with Duffy and Bedford that he expects Congress will look at a package more in the $10 billion to $30 billion range.

    In a recent development, for his part, Sen. Rick Scott, R-Fla., remarked the airline industry itself should foot at least a portion of the bill, considering how much federal support the carriers have received over the years.

    Sources indicate that “I don't understand why the airline industry doesn't pay for it. We give them unbelievable amounts of money,” Scott said, adding that he doesn’t like adding to the deficit and is “not significant on government running things.”.

    Duffy explained the need for the high price tag as the result of decades of pent-up demand that are now threatening major disruptions and safety risks to the traveling public.

    “This has never been done. To be clear, we are keeping planes safe in the sky, and we are switching out equipment that’s been a problem for decades,” he mentioned. “I and the president have decided we are going to lean in and fix it.”.

    Recent findings suggest that he called the effort a “historic investment” reflecting the ways air travel has changed since much of the nation’s infrastructure was built — noting that the newest tower was constructed in 1969 and much of the software being used is from the 1990s. Still, Duffy stated, on the current course of funding, it would take 300 years to replace every U.S. tower.

    Industry observers note that “I'm not going to tell [Congress] how to do their work, but I'm telling everybody what we need,” Duffy said. “And whether it's a party-line vote or if it's a bipartisan vote, I do think this is one moment in a very charged political environment — one moment where almost all Americans and bipartisan members of both bodies are kind of in agreement that we should lean in to do this.”.

    Even as Duffy petitioned for additional funds Tuesday, he noted that the “root cause” of the equipment instability that made the ground stop necessary is still unclear as investigators analyze the router that caused the problem.

    A “routine switchover” from old copper wires to digital fiber in the telecommunications system “started to create issues in our network,” Duffy explained Tuesday.

    Recent findings suggest that the telecommunications transition includes the conversion of thousands of routers to what are known as Juniper devices — a process being undertaken by contractor L3Harris Technologies. Duffy and Bedford explained that 68 other routers had been converted without incident prior to the problematic switchover Friday.

    Bedford remarked Tuesday that use of the router that officials have identified as the source of the system instability has been suspended “and we've disabled the ones that are out there.”.

    Industry observers note that the decision to suspend use of the router followed an inquiry sent to the agency by Senate Commerce Committee Democrats a day prior. “With thousands of conversions remaining, FAA must address outstanding safety and reliability concerns before expanding installation,” they wrote.

    Bedford said he was “highly confident” that similar problems wouldn’t erupt again. “Every element of this is going to be analyzed to see what we learn here and make sure that it doesn't get repeated,” he said.

    David Jordan, Lia Chien and Jacob Fulton contributed to this report.

    📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

    Marriott Bonvoy has just revealed its status soft landing policy for the next membership year, and it’s good news (well, at least for those who don’t requalify for their current status tier).

    Recent findings suggest that marriott Bonvoy has just revealed its status soft landing policy for the 2027 status year, for situations where someone doesn’t qualify for a particular elite tier based on their activity in 2026. Specifically, elite members who don’t achieve the published criteria to maintain their status will only drop down at most one elite tier.

    In other words, Ambassador Elites will at most drop to Titanium Elite, Titanium Elites will at most drop to Platinum Elite, Platinum Elites will at most drop to Gold Elite, and Gold Elites will drop at most to Silver Elite.

    For what it’s worth, this policy matches Marriott’s historical approach to status soft landings. Before Marriott and Starwood merged, back when Marriott’s loyalty program was named Marriott Rewards, Marriott consistently had a status soft landing policy. With this, Marriott Rewards members never dropped more than one elite tier per year, regardless of their activity.

    That policy has continued since the upcoming program was formed, including for the next year. However, there’s no guarantee this will continue to be the policy in the future. For those curious, the status offered as part of the soft landing also does count toward lifetime elite status. So if you’re downgraded from Titanium to Platinum based on a soft landing, that year of Platinum will add to your total.

    Sources indicate that during the pandemic, we saw airline and hotel loyalty programs largely extend elite status several times. This made sense, given the extent to which business travel decreased for many. However, with the huge increase in leisure travel and all the newly introduced ways to earn elite status, we’ve seen elite ranks swell.

    Personally I think the concept of a status soft landing makes a lot of sense. After all, sometimes life conditions change for people, and in many cases those changes are just temporary. If you drop from top tier status to no status, you don’t really have much of an incentive to stay loyal to that hotel group when your travel picks up again.

    It has been revealed that by offering a soft landing, loyalty programs can try to build more of a long term relationship with members, and that’s a positive. We also see some programs allow members to pause their status for a year or extend status as a one-time exception based on life circumstances, and I think that’s a great policy as well.

    Industry observers note that marriott Bonvoy has a generous status soft landing policy for 2027, for those who don’t requalify for status in 2026. If you didn’t requalify for your current status tier with Marriott Bonvoy in 2026, you can expect that you’ll be downgraded at most one status level.

    The Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card is one of the most compelling co-branded airline credit cards out there. I’m a huge fan of the Air Canada Aeroplan program — even if you have no connection to Air Canada or Aeroplan, the program is fantastic for partner redemptions, and this card is worth being aware of. And if you do fly Air Canada with any frequency, the perks for travel on the airline are strong.

    In a recent development, so this post is my in-depth Air Canada Aeroplan Card review. Let’s go over all the details, and discuss if the card is worth it.

    Link: Learn more about the Chase Air Canada Aeroplan® Credit Card.

    Before I review the Air Canada Aeroplan Card benefits in detail, here’s a high-level look at everything you need to know about the card:.

    Here are my thoughts on the Air Canada Aeroplan Card’s biggest pros and cons:.

    If you’re thinking about applying for the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card, you’re probably most interested in the welcome bonus it’s presently offering, along with its annual fee and general eligibility rules for getting the card. So let’s get into those details.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card currently has the following welcome bonus: Limited Time Offer: Earn up to 80,000 bonus points. Earn 60,000 bonus points after you spend $3,000 on purchases in the first 3 months your account is open. Plus, up to 20,000 more bonus points by earning 50% more bonus points per $1 spent on purchases that normally earn 1 bonus point in the first 2 months from account opening..

    Based on my latest miles & points valuations, I consider Aeroplan points to be worth 1.4 cents each. That means the 80,000 points are worth $1,120 to me. However, even if you have a different valuation of these points than I do, you can at least use the “Pay Yourself Back” feature to redeem these points for 1.25 cents each toward a travel purchase, so that’s a pretty high “cash out” value.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card is issued by Chase, and has pretty standard application restrictions:.

    Industry observers note that while Chase doesn’t have a public credit score requirement for the Air Canada Aeroplan Card, you’ll have the best chances of approval if your score is in the good range or higher. That roughly translates to a minimum score of 670. However, people have been approved with lower scores and rejected with higher scores, as it’s one of only many factors that determine card eligibility.

    Sources indicate that the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card has a $195 annual fee. There’s no cost to add authorized owners to the card, and their spending will count toward your points balance and any spending thresholds.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Card has no foreign transaction fees, so it’s a great card to use globally, and possibly even earn bonus rewards on your spending depending on what you’re using the card for.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Card has a well rounded rewards structure, among the most interesting you’ll find on any airline credit cards. This isn’t just about the number of points that you earn, but also about the additional rewards for spending. Specifically, the Aeroplan Card offers the following:.

    In a recent development, those are some excellent bonus categories. For what it’s worth, the card offers 1x Aeroplan points on all other purchases, so there are better cards for everyday spending.

    There’s a lot to love about Air Canada Aeroplan points, even if you don’t usually fly Air Canada or travel to Canada. Among other things:.

    I redeem miles through Aeroplan all the time, and consistently get great value. Booking award flights on Air Canada itself rather than other partners isn’t always the best deal, though, especially if you’re booking during a peak travel time, since Air Canada awards use dynamic pricing.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Card gives cardmembers plenty of opportunities to earn elite status with Air Canada Aeroplan. You get some status outright just for being a cardmember, and you can earn further status with spending.

    It has been revealed that those who are approved for the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card receive Aeroplan 25K status. This is valid for as long as your account is open. Aeroplan Elite 25K is Air Canada’s entry level status, and includes travel perks with Air Canada, including:.

This is automatic, but as I’ll cover below, you can stack additional credits on top through hitting certain spending thresholds in the calendar year.

    Sources indicate that beyond the automatic 5,000 SQCs you’ll receive each calendar year just for having the Air Canada Aeroplan Card, you can earn up to 20,000 additional credits by hitting spending thresholds. Here’s how that breaks down:.

    Whether or not that’s worth it really depends on how much you fly Air Canada, and what the opportunity cost of your credit card spending is.

    According to recent reports, those with the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card can get a one-tier status upgrade to Aeroplan 35K status when they spend $75,000 on the card in a calendar year. You’ll get status for the remainder of the calendar year you qualify and the entire following calendar year.

    In a recent development, if you ask me, the value here is really for someone who is actually loyal to Air Canada. Aeroplan 35K status gets you three complimentary checked bags on Air Canada flights (vs. just one with Aeroplan 25K), 10 eUpgrade credits, and a 3x elite points multiplier on eligible Air Canada or Star Alliance flight bookings, among other things.

    According to recent reports, the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a variety of valuable benefits and credits, beyond the elite status perks covered above. Some of these benefits are offered just for being a cardmember, while others can be earned with spending. The perks are pretty comprehensive, and you’ll find almost everything you could want short of lounge access. So let’s go over those.

    Recent findings suggest that the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers up to $100 in Air Canada statement credits when you make qualifying Air Canada purchases. The credits apply to paid airfare, taxes and fees on award flights, and inflight food and drinks, though onboard Wi-Fi is excluded.

    Sources indicate that this breaks down as two credits of up to $50 each, one from January 1 through June 30 and one from July 1 through December 31. If you book cash fares on Air Canada twice a year, this is an easy way to put $100 back in your pocket, and this benefit alone can cover about half of the card’s annual fee.

    Sources indicate that as an Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card holder, you can receive a 15% discount on the Aeroplan points required to book an award flight on Air Canada, Air Canada Express, or Air Canada Rouge. In practice, this also seems to work on partner award flights, as long as at least one segment is on Air Canada. The upside here can be absolutely huge, and it’s a great reason to have this card.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a free first checked bag on Air Canada flights for the primary cardmember and up to eight others traveling on the same itinerary. This applies to itineraries with Air Canada, Air Canada Rouge, or Air Canada Express. The value of that could add up pretty swiftly. There’s no need to actually pay for the ticket with the card, as long as you’re the primary cardmember and have your Aeroplan number linked to the reservation.

    Recent findings suggest that once every four years, the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers a credit that’s valid toward a membership with Global Entry, TSA PreCheck, or NEXUS, worth up to $120. These are all programs that can save travelers time at the airport, and potentially even at the border.

    I specifically love that the card also offers a NEXUS credit, since that’s historically something we haven’t seen card issuers offer. NEXUS is arguably the best of the three programs, since it gets you access to Global Entry, TSA PreCheck, and expedited immigration in Canada.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card is a World Elite Mastercard, which comes with certain perks, including a concierge service and presale tickets for eligible events.

    In a recent development, this is an incredibly innovative concept, and something that cardmembers may find to be valuable. So whether you want to redeem your points for a stay at a Four Seasons or a flight on JetBlue, the possibilities are endless. It’s also a reason to potentially think of the welcome bonus differently — the bonus points earned with the welcome offer can over time be redeemed toward any recent purchase or even toward the card’s annual fee.

    It has been revealed that the Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card also offers the ability to earn priority reward vouchers. Each can be used to get 50% off an eligible Aeroplan award ticket, and is valid for travel on Air Canada or a partner airline.

    As you can tell, the value here will depend on your status and travel patterns, but there’s potentially quite a bit of value to be had.

    Sources indicate that while this is something that most people won’t be able to achieve, I love the concept behind this, and for some it might just be the best deal in travel. The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card offers what I’d consider to be the world’s most valuable companion certificate, for those who spend a million dollars per year on the card.

    If you reach that threshold, you’ll receive an award redemption companion voucher that’s valid globally:.

    In a recent development, we’ve never seen a credit card offer a perk quite this valuable before. Obviously, the spending requirement is massive here, and this would only make sense if you were planning a lot of travel in a particular year. For a certain type of consumer, though, this is an incredible opportunity.

    Sources indicate that A few Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card benefits are set to expire on December 31, 2026, so they won’t be around for too much longer. Here’s a quick look:.

    The Air Canada Aeroplan Credit Card is an innovative product with a major welcome bonus, great return on spending, and valuable perks. That’s just about all that I look for in a credit card.

    According to recent reports, airline co-brand credit cards are extremely popular given the allegiance many people have to a particular airline. Admittedly Aeroplan is at a disadvantage in the US market, since not as many people in the US are loyal to Air Canada as they are to American, Delta, or United, for example.

    Recent findings suggest that that being said, I think the thoughtful value proposition of this card more than makes up for it for Air Canada loyalists. If you like to redeem points for international premium cabin awards, it could be worth applying for this card. Similarly, the card can be worth it for the Pay Yourself Back feature, whereby you can redeem your Aeroplan points however you’d like toward a travel purchase.

    Hopefully most people find value beyond just the bonus, given the excellent rewards structure.

Aeroplan is transfer partners with several bank currencies, including Amex Membership Rewards, Bilt Rewards, Capital One, and Chase Ultimate Rewards, and all those currencies can be converted at a 1:1 ratio.
